dietEvidence.body: Herbivory is inferred from sauropod anatomy and the associated flora. The plant fossils show what grew in the environment; they are not gut contents and do not establish the diet.

sizeNote: Length and mass are published estimates, not measurements of a complete individual. Length estimates range from about 24 to 34 m and mass estimates from about 29 to 50 t; the skull and most of the tail are unknown.
tagline: A large titanosaur with a relatively complete axial skeleton. It helps document the anatomy of titanosaur necks and pelves.
summary: A large titanosaur with a relatively complete axial skeleton. It helps document the anatomy of titanosaur necks and pelves.

discovery.body: Named by Calvo, Porfiri, González Riga and Kellner in 2007 from the Portezuelo Formation at Lake Barreales, Neuquén, Argentina. The holotype, MUCPv-323, preserves a complete neck, dorsal vertebrae and ribs, sacrum, pelvis and one anterior caudal vertebra, but not the skull, forelimbs or most of the tail.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: The holotype, MUCPv-323, is one of the most complete giant sauropod skeletons known, preserving a complete neck, dorsal vertebrae, ribs, sacrum, pelvis and one anterior caudal. The skull and most of the tail are missing.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: The Portezuelo Formation, Neuquén, records the species in the Turonian–Coniacian. The numeric range used here is ≈94–86 Ma, an occurrence estimate rather than a direct date on every specimen.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The neck is long, the dorsal vertebrae are pneumatised, and the pelvis is wide; the preserved sacrum is exceptionally large. The skull is unknown.

behaviour.body: Herbivory is inferred from sauropod anatomy. The quarry preserves a diverse flora and fauna, but no nesting, social or migratory behaviour is recorded.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from a partial skeleton including much of the axial column and pelvis; the skull and most of the tail are unknown. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: The holotype is exceptionally complete for a giant sauropod, but it lacks the skull, forelimbs and most of the tail. Size estimates vary widely, and the plants from the quarry are environmental evidence, not gut contents.
